title: the account lost 25 media in a BOUNDED event inside the last 26h (now 200); the inventory has held for 7.7h
evidence: platform media_count=200 (0.7h ago) -- down 25 between two consecutive snapshots inside the last 26h. Publishing can only INCREASE media_count, so this many media were removed (or archived) on the platform side. This app believes it has published 150 post(s) with a provider id, and nothing local is re-checked after publish: a removed post still counts as posted in the queue runway, the 14-day acceptance counter and the per-pillar engagement read. Per-post re-read (`bin/rake instagram:media_inventory`, 200 media listed): 36 of our 150 published post(s) are ABSENT from the account; gone post ids: 136,133,134,135,138,139,140,141,142,143,148,307. Removals are NOT ongoing: the inventory has held at 200 across the last 10 consecutive snapshot(s), spanning 7.7h, so this is a bounded event rather than active suppression. A gone media answers GET /{media-id}?fields=id with HTTP 400, code 100, subcode 33, while a live one answers 200 -- that is how the set above was established. Producer: Growth::MetricsCollector#fetch_media_count, hourly via growth:snapshot_followers, best effort by design (a failed call stores NULL, never 0); per-post via bin/rake instagram:media_inventory (read-only).

notes.note: 2026-09-24 22:3xZ ops-triage: DETECTOR FIXED, DURABLE RECORD MOVED. Root cause of the removals is platform-side and unreadable from here (36 of our 150 published posts are gone; 25 in one burst 18:00-21:00Z today) -- carried as its own item, platform-removals-cause-unknown, routed tim for the one fact only a login can supply (Account Status). What was WRONG IN THIS REPO was that the removal was invisible and this check could never close: (a) bin/rake instagram:media_inventory is new -- read-only, aborts on a broken read instead of printing 0, lists the account media ids and names the posts of ours that are absent (listed=200 ours=150 missing=36); (b) this check now also fires on posts of ours newly missing, watermarked in ops/media_inventory.json so it re-opens on the NEXT removal and not every tick (1st run: newly_missing=36; 2nd: 0); (c) the stock condition no longer compares against an ALL-TIME max(media_count) -- that re-fired on every tick forever after one historical removal, i.e. an item that could be filed and never closed. It now measures a decrease between two CONSECUTIVE snapshots inside a 26h window: verified against the live DB, it reads 'media_count fell by 25 inside the last 26h (now 200)' and goes silent once the readings stop falling (from 2026-09-25 23:00Z). Selftest 734/0. This item is the live detector and will auto-close; the forensic numbers and the ask live on platform-removals-cause-unknown.

2026-09-25 03:3xZ ops-triage: ROOT FIX COMPLETED -- the HEADLINE, not just the evidence, now brackets the event. Last pass added the trend clause to the evidence but left the headline 'media_count fell by 25 inside the last 26h', which this check's own docstring called out as the real trap (genome: Point-Reading != Event): it stays literally true for a full day after the wave, so a reader skimming the board reads a finished purge as ongoing. New PURE media_removed_headline(drop, newest, window_h, rows) picks the verb from media_stability_verdict -- STILL SHRINKING while the readings fall; 'lost N media in a BOUNDED event ... held for Hh' once they hold; and the old literal wording ONLY when the history is unreadable (never guess from no data). Live read this tick: 'the account lost 25 media in a BOUNDED event inside the last 26h (now 200); the inventory has held for 6.5h'. Verified: selftest 779/0 (was 774, +5 cases: flat/bounded, bounded-not-SHRANK, falling, unreadable-keeps-literal, no-drop->None); checks-audit 65 checks, 0 raised, 0 unreadable. The item stays OPEN as the live detector -- it self-closes when the 26h window rolls past the removals (~2026-09-25 23:00Z) and reopens on the next removal.
